steps.message:
The change is a one-line edit, but it crosses an API boundary, so I'm stopping before touching it.

`routes/users.js:6` emits `userId` in the `GET /users` response body. That field name is the contract, not an internal detail. `README.md` names three consumers — the web app, the iOS app (3.2+), and the nightly partner export — and states that field-name changes go through a versioned endpoint. Renaming it in place breaks all three at once, and the shipped iOS clients can't be fixed forward. The `/orders` handler on line 12 already uses `user_id`, so the inconsistency is real; it's the delivery mechanism that's the problem.

options.description: Return `userId` and `user_id` side by side in the /users response. Nothing breaks, consumers migrate at their own pace, and `userId` gets removed later once all three are off it. Additive and reversible.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Leave /users as-is and add a v2 (or equivalent) that returns `user_id`. Matches what the README says the process is, but is more than a field rename in scope.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Replace `userId` with `user_id` on /users as originally asked. Immediately breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated; shipped iOS clients cannot be fixed forward.
